analysis.investment_thesis: Meesho is a loss-deepening internet marketplace with no earnings, a promoter holding of just 16.57%, and equity eroding from ₹2,472 Cr to ₹1,446 Cr in two years — the exact opposite of what I look for. At P/B of 50x on a business with negative ROE of -264%, the market is pricing in a future I cannot verify or quantify with confidence.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at ~28% CAGR (FY23-25), showing some marketplace traction in Tier 2/3 India
Operating cash flow turned positive in FY24-25 (₹220 Cr and ₹539 Cr respectively) — early sign of unit economics improving
Minimal debt (D/E of 0.09) — balance sheet is not leveraged, giving runway
key_risks: Net loss exploded to ₹3,942 Cr in FY25 vs ₹328 Cr in FY24 — losses are not narrowing, they are widening dramatically
Promoter stake of only 16.57% is disqualifying — no meaningful skin in the game from those who built it
Equity book value collapsing (₹2,472 Cr → ₹1,446 Cr) while the stock commands P/B of 50x — destruction of intrinsic value
red_flags: ROE of -264% and ROCE of -8.71% — capital is being destroyed at an alarming rate
Other income swung to -₹835 Cr in FY25 from +₹231 Cr in FY24, suggesting large write-downs or investment losses
Financing CF of +₹2,105 Cr in FY25 — company is surviving on fresh capital raises, not organic cash generation
No dividend history, no earnings history — purely a speculative growth story
Operating margin of -15.63% shows the core business is still deeply uneconomical
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I built DMart by finding businesses where the economics were simple and proven — low margins, high turns, and customers who came back every week because the value was undeniable. Meesho is the polar opposite of that model. The FY25 net loss of ₹3,942 Cr on revenues of ₹9,390 Cr tells me that for every ₹100 of revenue, this business is destroying roughly ₹42 in net value. The improvement in operating cash flow to ₹539 Cr is noted, but the investing outflow of ₹2,638 Cr and the need to raise ₹2,105 Cr in financing tells the real story — this machine burns cash faster than it earns it, and outside investors are the ones keeping it alive.

The promoter holding of 16.57% is disqualifying on its own. I have always believed that promoters who have built something great don't sell down below 50% — they want to own as much as they can. When the people who know this business best hold only 16%, and the equity base is shrinking from ₹2,472 Cr to ₹1,446 Cr while the market cap sits at ₹74,700 Cr, the gap between price and reality is dangerous. At P/B of 50x on negative book value trajectory, this stock demands perfection in execution for the next decade. I prefer businesses where I don't need perfection — just consistency. Meesho offers neither today.
